$$
x=2t-1,\,\,\,y=2-{t}^{2},\,-3\le t\le 3.
$$

Determine the graph of the following parametrically defined curve:

$$
x=t+2,\qquad y=1-t,\qquad -2\leq t\leq 2.
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Create a table of paired coordinates. First calculate the $x$-values:

| $t$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| $y$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Now calculate the $y$-values at the same parameter values:

| $t$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ | $4$ |
| $y$ | $3$ | $2$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-1$ |

The paired coordinates are $(0,3)$, $(1,2)$, $(2,1)$, $(3,0)$ and $(4,-1)$. They lie on a decreasing straight line. Keep only the segment from $(0,3)$ to $(4,-1)$, with both endpoints included. A line with the right slope but different endpoints is not the required graph.

![The curve through the calculated points](images/82/8227fb9f808f8b7622b2d3910efa11ce6d87b8085b4d7e24a77a342306532ee4.png)

:question/problem:
Determine the graph of the following parametrically defined curve:

$$
x=t^2-1,\qquad y=2-t,\qquad -1\leq t\leq 2.
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Create a table of paired coordinates. First calculate the $x$-values:

| $t$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $3$ |
| $y$ |  |  |  |  |

Now calculate the $y$-values at the same parameter values:

| $t$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $3$ |
| $y$ | $3$ | $2$ | $1$ | $0$ |

The points are $(0,3)$, $(-1,2)$, $(0,1)$ and $(3,0)$. As $t$ runs from $-1$ to $0$, $x$ decreases to $-1$; as $t$ runs from $0$ to $2$, $x$ increases to $3$. Meanwhile $y$ decreases throughout. Plot the smooth right-opening arc through these points. Its leftmost point is $(-1,2)$, and its included endpoints are $(0,3)$ and $(3,0)$. The two arms have different lengths because the parameter interval is asymmetric.

![The curve through the calculated points](images/93/9346e80ef10f528dd956f6d11b511b106e39c9d2724a6be0c6e60f9e73afe183.png)

:question/problem:
Determine the graph of the following parametrically defined curve:

$$
x=t(t-2),\qquad y=t(t+2),\qquad -2\leq t\leq 2.
$$
:question/worked-solution:
Create a table of paired coordinates. First calculate the $x$-values:

| $t$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $8$ | $3$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $0$ |
| $y$ |  |  |  |  |  |

Now calculate the $y$-values at the same parameter values:

| $t$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x$ | $8$ | $3$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $0$ |
| $y$ | $0$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $3$ | $8$ |

The successive points are $(8,0)$, $(3,-1)$, $(0,0)$, $(-1,3)$ and $(0,8)$. Both coordinates turn within the interval: $x=(t-1)^2-1$ has minimum $-1$ at $t=1$, while $y=(t+1)^2-1$ has minimum $-1$ at $t=-1$. Plot a smooth curve through the paired points in parameter order. It dips below the $x$-axis through $(3,-1)$, passes through the origin, then bends left of the $y$-axis through $(-1,3)$ before reaching $(0,8)$. All five choices share the endpoints and the origin, so those three checkpoints alone cannot decide the answer. Check both interior bends.

![The curve through the calculated points](images/86/8644be497d26e662b3b867539ee7b8d0dd812fac915e55db7b05045592a4fc6e.png)
